{
  "problem": "Design a minimal REST API for task management that supports basic CRUD operations.",
  "objectives": [
    "Define a minimal set of endpoints for basic task operations (create, read, update, delete).",
    "Specify the HTTP methods and URL structures for each endpoint.",
    "Outline the expected request/response formats in JSON.",
    "Ensure the design is simple and focused on core CRUD functionality."
  ],
  "deliverables": [
    "A list of API endpoints with their HTTP methods and URL patterns.",
    "A description of the request body for POST and PUT endpoints.",
    "A description of the response body for GET, POST, and PUT endpoints.",
    "A description of the response for successful DELETE operation.",
    "A definition of the standard JSON structure for error responses."
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "The API must be RESTful.",
    "It must be minimal, avoiding unnecessary complexity.",
    "It must use standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) appropriately.",
    "All responses must follow a consistent JSON structure."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A 'task' object has fields: id (UUID), title (string), description (string), status (string, e.g., 'pending', 'in-progress', 'completed'), created_at (ISO timestamp), updated_at (ISO timestamp).",
    "The API supports listing all tasks via a GET endpoint.",
    "The API does not require versioning (no /v1/ prefix).",
    "Error responses will use a consistent format: {\"error\": \"message\"}.",
    "The API is stateless and does not handle authentication or authorization."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Implement advanced features like authentication, pagination, or filtering.",
    "Define a backend technology stack or database schema.",
    "Specify deployment or hosting details.",
    "Provide client-side code or SDKs."
  ],
  "acceptance": [
    "The API includes endpoints for creating, reading (single and list), updating, and deleting tasks.",
    "Each endpoint uses the correct HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).",
    "Request and response bodies are well-defined JSON structures.",
    "The API design is minimal and focuses only on core task CRUD operations.",
    "Error responses follow a consistent JSON format."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "The minimal design may not cover all use cases (e.g., bulk operations).",
    "Lack of versioning could cause issues if the API evolves later.",
    "No authentication may limit security in a production environment."
  ]
}
